learn.title: Secrets, certificates and keys: Key Vault and Managed HSM
objectives: Choose between Key Vault Standard, Key Vault Premium, Managed HSM and Cloud HSM for a set of requirements
Design access to vaults with Azure RBAC and managed identities, using least privilege
Protect vault contents with soft delete, purge protection, network isolation and logging
Design rotation and expiry for keys, secrets and certificates, including auto-renewal with integrated CAs
Recommend customer-managed keys and double encryption for Azure Storage, Azure SQL and managed disks
concepts: Key Vault Standard
Multi-tenant vault for secrets, certificates and software-protected keys. The cheapest option when HSM protection is not required.
Key Vault Premium
Adds HSM-protected keys (RSA-HSM, EC-HSM) on multi-tenant, FIPS 140 Level 3 validated HSMs. Secrets cost the same as Standard.
Managed HSM
Fully managed, single-tenant HSM pool for keys only. The customer owns the security domain and grants data access through local RBAC.
Azure Cloud HSM
Single-tenant HSM that the customer administers, for lift-and-shift apps that use PKCS#11, JCE, CNG or OpenSSL. Mention level for AZ-305.
Soft delete
Always on for new vaults. Deleted vaults and objects stay recoverable for 7 to 90 days (90 by default), and the vault name stays reserved.
Purge protection
Blocks purging until the retention period ends. You cannot turn it off once it is on, and customer-managed keys for Storage, SQL and disks require it.
Azure RBAC for Key Vault
The recommended permission model. Data-plane roles such as Key Vault Secrets User can be scoped to a vault or to a single object.
Key rotation policy
Rotates keys automatically on a schedule and can notify through Event Grid before expiry. Secrets have no native rotation, so use Event Grid and a Function.
Key Vault references
App Service, Functions and Container Apps read secrets through a managed identity. A versionless reference picks up new versions automatically.
Customer-managed key (CMK)
A key in Key Vault or Managed HSM that wraps a service's data encryption key. Revoking access to it makes the data unreadable.
Double encryption
Two layers at rest: storage infrastructure encryption, which you choose at account creation, or a disk encryption set that uses platform and customer keys.
Trusted Microsoft services
A firewall exception that lets services such as Azure Storage and Azure SQL reach a restricted vault for CMK. It does not cover App Service Key Vault references.
comparisons: Both store secrets and certificates at the same price. Choose Premium only when keys must be HSM-protected or you need BYOK from an on-premises HSM.

Premium uses shared HSMs and Microsoft-run administration. Managed HSM is single-tenant, the customer controls the security domain, it supports symmetric AES keys, but it holds no secrets or certificates.
Managed HSM integrates with Azure services for CMK. Cloud HSM gives full HSM administration to IaaS apps that use standard HSM APIs.
Access policies apply only at vault level, and anyone with Contributor can grant themselves data access. RBAC separates the control plane from the data plane and supports per-object scope.
A private endpoint with public access disabled removes internet exposure. Firewall rules with service endpoints still expose a public endpoint, just restricted to allowed sources.
Built-in replication vs your own second vault
Built-in paired-region replication fails over automatically but is read-only. A separate vault per region gives independent, writable regions but you must sync it yourself.
traps: Key Vault Contributor and Key Vault Reader do not grant access to secret values under the RBAC model.
Managed HSM cannot store secrets or certificates. Pair it with a vault if you need them.
Activity logs do not show data-plane operations such as reading or deleting a secret. Enable AuditEvent resource logs in advance.
App Service is not a trusted service for Key Vault references. A locked-down vault needs VNet integration and a private endpoint.
Soft delete keeps a deleted vault's name reserved, so redeploying with the same name fails until the vault is recovered or purged.
Backups can be restored only to a vault in the same subscription and the same Azure geography.
revision: Use one vault per application, per environment, per region.
Prefer managed identities, and where the target service supports Entra authentication, remove the secret entirely.
Turn on purge protection for any vault that holds customer-managed keys.
Use versionless key and secret references so rotation needs no configuration changes.
Let DigiCert or GlobalSign renew public certificates automatically. With other CAs, merge a CSR and set email notifications.
Use Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User for service identities that only wrap and unwrap keys.
Cache secrets in the application to avoid Key Vault throttling.
Send AuditEvent logs to Log Analytics and turn on Microsoft Defender for Key Vault to detect unusual access.

questions.q: True or false: after purge protection is enabled on a key vault, a Key Vault Administrator can disable it again.
opts: False. Purge protection cannot be disabled once it is enabled
False. Only the subscription Owner can disable it
True. Any Key Vault Administrator can disable it

questions.e: Purge protection is irreversible, so no deleted vault or object can be purged before its retention period ends.
